newsitem.title: USA: Edison cuts San Onofre 3 nuke output - NRC.
newsitem.headline: Edison cuts San Onofre 3 nuke output - NRC.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison Co reduced output at the San Onofre 3 nuclear unit after a control rod assembly dropped into the reactor core, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Friday.
Output at unit in San Clemente, Calif., was reduced to 46 percent of its 1,080 megawatt (MW) capacity, NRC said.
The commission, in its daily status report, said the cause of the incident was unknown, and that the assembly has been retrieved to its original position.
The adjoining San Onofre 2, rated at 1,070 MW, was operating at full output. The unit is scheduled to shut November 30 for a 70-day refueling.
Edison has a 75 percent ownership in the San Onofre units, while San Diego Gas and Electric Co, a subsidiary of Enova Corp, owns 20 percent and two municipal utilities own the remaining five percent.
